newsitem.title: POLAND: INTERVIEW - Agros eyes new opportunities.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Agros eyes new opportunities.

text.p: Polish food producer and trader Agros Holding SA will focus on its core business of fruit and vegetable processing but eyes some new food processing ventures to diversify risk, the company's president said on Saturday.
Zofia Gaber said the firm's 1997-98 investment programme envisaged strengthening Agros's position by restructuring its subsidaries, making them more efficient and buying new units.
She did not give the amount of the planned investment.

Agros has stakes in about 20 firms including majority stakes in eight fruit and vegetable processing companies and five subsidiaries dealing with farming, grain processing, confectionery and dairy production.
Gaber said milk processing, edible fats production, farming and confectionery seemed promising sectors but declined to name any specific companies which Agros was targeting.
"We are continuously analyzing opportunities ... there are fewer than 10 companies which we are considering and I think we will finalize two or three firms," she said.
She said half of the 1997-98 investment programme would be partly financed from a new issue of 2,425,000 shares planned for the first quarter of 1997.
The company expected to raise about 150 million zlotys from the issue. The remaining funds for the investment programme would come from own funds.
Gaber said she believed the investments would help strengthen both domestic and international position of Agros.
"We want to become and we are becoming a big, stable trading corporation, active in this part of Europe, able to compete with international firms," she said.

She said Agros group net profit was expected to rise to 48.5 million zlotys in 1996, up from last year's 38.5 million zlotys, while its group sales were seen rising to 1.3 billion zlotys, against 995 million zlotys last year.
She added the company expected to maintain a 10 percent growth in sales in real terms in the next two years.
Gaber said the new share issue was in part directed to foreign institutional investors, but said the company did not plan offering a strategic stake to any of the future investors.
"There are many investment banks, funds interested in our shares ... we would like to have several, passive investors," she said.

The issue is divided into three tranches, of yet undetermined size, to be offered to current shareholders, selected large, mainly foreign investors and the general public. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
